Here is a Semgrep rule that matches the vulnerable behavior and avoids matching the patched behavior:

```yaml
---
id: vuln-felix-dev-87513ea3
title: Apache Felix WebConsole Unsafe JavaScript Encoding
description: Apache Felix WebConsole does not properly sanitize user input before embedding it in a JavaScript context. This can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.
severity: WARNING
language: java

patterns:
  - name: unsafe-javascript-encoding
    meta:
      category: Security, Coding Standard
      confidence: High
    locations:
      - path: "org/apache/felix/webconsole/internal/core/ServicesServlet.java"
        lines:
          - begin: 20
            end: 21
---
```

This rule will match the vulnerable behavior where user-supplied input is not properly sanitized before being embedded in a JavaScript context, which can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. The `unsafe-javascript-encoding` pattern matches lines 20 and 21 of the file `ServicesServlet.java`.

Please note that this rule does not specify any specific taint-mode fields as it is a general rule for Apache Felix WebConsole. If you want to use Semgrep with a specific repository, you may need to adjust this rule accordingly.
